title: Adding a Member
how_it_works_companion: How It Works chapter 6, section HOW NEW MEMBERS ARE ADDED

sections.business_context:
Adding a member is the most consequential creation flow in the platform. It writes a login account, a
member profile, contact details, insurance, and a membership package, and it commits the club to a
payment schedule. Getting it wrong produces a duplicate identity, a member number that should
never have been issued, or a billing arrangement that does not match what was sold.
This guide covers the wizard that does it: what each step captures, what is written and when, how
duplicates are caught, and the difference between saving a member and activating one.
The single most important idea is that saving and activating are separate events. A saved member
has an identity and can be worked on. An activated member has a number, a start date, and a bill.
The gap between them is deliberate, because the club sells memberships that do not begin the day
they are agreed.
Pairs with How It Works chapter 6, section HOW NEW MEMBERS ARE ADDED.
sections.schema_overview:
TABLES WRITTEN BY THIS FLOW

Table                             What the wizard writes

USER                              The login account, created with the member profile in one transaction.

MEMBER                            The profile: names, license, date of birth, home branch, lifecycle status.

MEMBER_PHONE                      One or more numbers, typed, with an SMS opt-in.

MEMBER_EMAIL                      One or more addresses, typed, with three subscription flags.

MEMBER_ADDRESS                    One or more addresses, typed by purpose, location, and dwelling style.

MEMBER_INSURANCE_POLICY           The member’s policy, captured but never gating activation.

MEMBER_PACKAGE                    The membership period, its level, and its terms.

MEMBER_PAYMENT_SCHEDULE The dues arrangement agreed at activation.

MEMBER_BRANCH_HISTORY             The opening home branch row.


The wizard is a single logical transaction across several screens. Nothing is half-written: either the
member exists with everything the step captured, or the step did not happen.
sections.implementation_workflow:
1) Capturing the Person
    1. Capture first_name, last_name, and optionally middle_name and preferred_name.
       preferred_name is what greetings and displays use, falling back to first_name when it is
       empty.
    2. Capture date_of_birth. It is used for compliance and for age-related eligibility, and it is one of
       the fields duplicate detection compares.


    3. Capture the driving license: license_number, license_state resolving to STATE_SELECT, and
       license_expires_on. A member who will drive needs all three.
    4. Set home_branch_id. This is the location that serves the member, and it supplies the branch
       segment of the member number when one is minted.
    5. Set lifecycle_status to Pending. A member being entered is not yet active, whatever the intent.

2) Checking for a Duplicate
    1. Run duplicate detection before the profile is written, not after. A duplicate caught at save is a
       duplicate the club has to merge.
    2. Compare on normalized values: strip punctuation and case from names, reduce phone
       numbers to digits, and compare addresses on street number and postal code rather than on
       the whole string.
    3. A match on driving license number, or on an email address, is strong enough on its own to
       raise a flag.
    4. A match on any two of last name, date of birth, phone number, and street address is also
       enough to raise a flag.
    5. Flag rather than block. Two people genuinely do share a name and a birthday, and the person
       entering the record is better placed to judge than the system is.
    6. Where the match is a former member, route to the rejoin path rather than creating a second
       identity. Where it is a household member, offer the sharing arrangement instead.

EXAMPLE — WHAT RAISES A DUPLICATE FLAG

Signal                        On its own       Combined

Driving license number        Flags            —

Email address                 Flags            —

Last name                     No               Any two of these four flag

Date of birth                 No               Any two of these four flag

Phone number                  No               Any two of these four flag

Street address                No               Any two of these four flag



3) Capturing Contact Details
    1. Write MEMBER_PHONE rows with a type of Home, Work, Mobile, Assistant, Family, or
       Emergency. Mark exactly one primary. Capture sms_opt_in per number, because consent
       belongs to the number rather than to the person.
    2. Write MEMBER_EMAIL rows with a type and the three subscription flags: account_opt_in,
       vehicle_opt_in, and marketing_opt_in. At least one address must carry account and at least
       one must carry vehicle; marketing is optional.
    3. The email column is citext, so comparison is case-insensitive and no normalization is needed
       on write.
    4. Write MEMBER_ADDRESS rows typed by purpose, by location, and by dwelling style. The
       style matters for delivery: a high-rise and a detached house need different arrangements.
    5. Do not mark an address primary; no such flag exists. Where mailing and physical differ, both
       are captured as separate rows rather than as two halves of one, and a reservation names the
       address a delivery or collection uses.

4) Capturing Insurance
    1. Capture the policy and its coverages. The detail belongs to the insurance guide in group C of
       this chapter.
    2. Insurance never gates activation. A member can be activated, billed, and given a number
       without a verified policy on file.
    3. The layered model in full: missing insurance never blocks booking; a policy known to have
       expired blocks new reservations until replaced (see the insurance guide); checkout always
       requires current coverage.
    4. What insurance gates is vehicle release. A member without current coverage cannot take a
       car, and that check lives in the reservation flow.
    5. This separation is deliberate and is easy to get backwards. Blocking activation on insurance
       would stop the club billing a member who has agreed to join.

5) Capturing the Membership
    1. Write the MEMBER_PACKAGE row with its membership level, its start and end dates, and a
       status of Draft. The wizard saves freely into Draft.
    2. Only levels available at the enrolling branch may be offered. Availability is read from
       MEMBERSHIP_LEVEL_BRANCH_AVAILABILITY, never from the access table.
    3. Write MEMBER_PAYMENT_SCHEDULE from the level’s pricing at the enrolling branch,
       effective on the enrollment date.
    4. Dues doctrine applies without exception: no proration ever, always the first of the month,
       twelve equal payments in twelve successive months, with month one paid at joining.
    5. Sharing members and additional drivers are captured as participants. That structure belongs
       to group B of this chapter.

6) Saving Versus Activating
    1. On save, the member exists with a member_id and a lifecycle_status of Pending. No member
       number is minted and no member_since date is set.
    2. Activation requires a payment arrangement in place and no outstanding hold. Insurance is not
       a prerequisite.
    3. On first activation, mint member_seq and member_number, set member_since, and move
       lifecycle_status to Active. All four happen together or none of them do.
    4. A member who is never activated keeps their member_id and never receives a number. This
       is correct, and it is why the number sequence has permanent gaps.
    5. An activation task is raised seven days ahead of the start date and is due on the start date.
       Where a package is created inside that window, raise it immediately. Nothing activates
       automatically; a person confirms.
    6. If the planned start date is edited, move the task with it. A task due on a date that no longer
       means anything sits overdue while the real start is still weeks away.



    7. Activation sets the start date, in both directions. Late activation moves the start forward; early
       activation moves it back to the activation date. The planned date is a plan and the moment of
       activation is what governs.
    8. The originally planned date is preserved in the package’s change history, so the difference
       between what was intended and what happened stays answerable.
    9. A gift set to start on a birthday is therefore activated on the birthday, never before, because
       activating early would begin the year early.
    10. Activation also posts any joining bonus onto the package and converts any tentative
        reservations held against the member into confirmed ones. That conversion is what makes a
        birthday delivery work: staff book it against the Pending member, and activation makes it real.

EXAMPLE — WHAT EXISTS AT EACH STAGE

                              Saved (Pending)   Activated

member_id                     Yes               Yes

member_number                 No                Yes, minted at first activation

member_since                  No                Yes

lifecycle_status              Pending           Active

Payment schedule              Written           Running

Can take a vehicle            No                Only with current insurance
sections.rules_and_constraints:
1. The account and the member profile are created in one transaction.
    2. MEMBER.user_id is unique; one login account carries at most one member profile.
    3. Duplicate detection runs before the profile is written and flags rather than blocks.
    4. A license or email match flags on its own; any two of last name, date of birth, phone, and
       street address flag together.
    5. At least one email address carries the account flag and at least one carries the vehicle flag.
    6. Exactly one phone and exactly one email per member is marked primary - the number the club
       calls first and the address a screen shows when it has room for one. The interface requires
       one of each; the database enforces at most one, since no constraint can compel a row to
       exist. Addresses carry no primary: a member keeps a home and an office and neither is more
       correct, so the reservation names the address a delivery goes to rather than the member
       record nominating one in advance.
    7. Only membership levels available at the enrolling branch may be offered.
    8. Insurance never gates activation and always gates vehicle release.
    9. Activation requires a payment arrangement and no hold.
    10. Activation sets the start date in both directions; the originally planned date is preserved in the
        change history.
    11. Activation posts any joining bonus and converts tentative reservations held against the
        member.
    12. The activation task is due on the start date and moves whenever that date is edited.
    13. member_seq, member_number, and member_since are set at first activation and never
        before.
    14. Dues are never prorated, always fall on the first, and run as twelve equal payments.
    15. A never-activated member holds an identity and no number.
sections.integration_and_edge_cases:
1. A former member rejoining. Duplicate detection should catch them. Route to the rejoin path,
       which reuses the existing member record and its original number rather than creating a
       second identity.
    2. A member being added by someone at another branch. The enrolling branch decides
       which levels are on offer and which prices apply. The member’s home branch may differ, and
       that is a separate field.
    3. A member who never activates. Legitimate. They hold an identity, appear in searches, and
       have no number. Do not treat the missing number as an error.
    4. A household sharing one email address. The uniqueness is on the login account, not on the
       member email row, so two members may list the same address. Only one of them can use it to
       sign in.
    5. A member with no driving license. Possible where the membership is held by someone who
       never drives, with an additional driver doing the driving. Do not require it.
    6. Activation before the planned start date. The start moves back to the activation date, the
       end date and payment schedule recompute, and the membership year begins now. Activating
       a future-dated gift early is therefore a mistake rather than a convenience.
    7. Activation after the start date. The start moves forward, and the end date and payment
       schedule are recomputed, so the member receives their full year rather than losing the days
       nobody used. Staff confirm rather than the system deciding.
    8. A tentative reservation against a Pending member. Converts at activation. Where the
       member never activates, the reservation falls with the enrollment.
    9. A duplicate flag ignored deliberately. Two genuine people. Record that the flag was
       reviewed, so the next person to notice does not investigate it again.
sections.automations_and_notifications:
Each automation below is listed with its trigger and its expected outcome. Operational specification is
reserved for the automations pass that follows the first draft of all chapters.

AUTOMATIONS IN THIS GUIDE

Trigger                            Outcome

Member saved                       Login account created; invitation sent to the primary account-flagged address.

Duplicate flag raised              Entry pauses for review; the matching records are shown side by side.

                                   Activation task raised for staff, due on the start date. Nothing activates
Seven days before the start date
                                   automatically.

Planned start date edited          Activation task due date moves with it.


Trigger                           Outcome

First activation                  Member number and member_since minted; welcome correspondence sent.

Late activation confirmed         Start date moved forward; end date and payment schedule recomputed.

Insurance missing at activation   Member activated and billed; vehicle release blocked until coverage is on file.


Reserved for the automations pass: welcome correspondence content and routing, activation task
assignment, and whether a duplicate flag notifies anyone beyond the person entering the record.
sections.developer_notes:
1. One transaction, several screens. The wizard spans steps but commits as a unit. A partial
       write leaves a member the club cannot bill and cannot find.
    2. Normalize before comparing. Duplicate detection on raw strings finds almost nothing. Strip
       case and punctuation from names, reduce phones to digits, and compare addresses on
       number and postal code.
    3. Flag, never block. A blocking duplicate check will be worked around by entering a middle
       initial, which produces exactly the duplicate it was meant to prevent.
    4. Minting is atomic. member_seq, member_number, member_since, and the status change
       happen together. A number issued without a status change is a number the club cannot
       explain.
    5. Never mint on save. The gap between a saved and an activated member is the reason the
       number sequence has gaps, and those gaps are correct.
    6. Insurance is not a gate here. Any code that refuses activation for missing insurance has
       inverted the rule and will stop the club billing members who have agreed to join.
    7. Availability, not access. Enrollment reads which levels may be sold at this branch. Reading
       the access table instead offers levels the branch cannot sell.
    8. citext on the email column. No lower-casing on write, and comparison is already case-
       insensitive.
